transcript.content: Hi, welcome in — I'm Dr. Lee. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Lee. Well, I guess what brought me in is... I just don't feel like myself anymore. I've noticed I barely talk to people lately. I just kind of go flat and quiet. And work is getting really tough. I'm a building cleaner, and honestly, even just getting started on my cleaning route feels like pushing a loaded cart uphill. I just can't seem to get going.
How long have you been feeling this way—flat, quiet, and low on energy—has it been a matter of weeks, or has it been going on for a year or more?
It's been going on for a while. Definitely more than a few weeks. I'd say... probably about a year and two months now. Yeah, it started up not long after I moved.

Over this past year and two months, has this low, flat feeling been present almost every day without much of a break, or have there been stretches—days or weeks—where you felt more like your usual self?

Honestly, it's been pretty much every day without a break. For most of the time since the move, the sadness and the low energy... and just feeling guilty and losing interest in things, it's all just been there in the background. Even on the days when the voices, or... or my worries about the cameras are the main thing on my mind, that low feeling is still right there underneath it all. I haven't really had any stretches where I felt like my usual self.
You mentioned hearing voices and worrying about cameras — did those experiences start around the same time as the low mood and flatness, or did they begin before or after that?
Well, they didn't start right away. The low mood was first. I'd say the voices and... the worries about being watched, those started a little later. They've been going on for about 11 months now.
Since the voices and worries about being watched began, has there been any period of at least two weeks where you experienced those symptoms but did NOT feel low, flat, or down in mood?

Well, let me think... yeah, actually, there was a time. There was a stretch of several weeks where my mood had lifted a bit. I was getting through my meals and doing my work cleaning the building a little better than usual. But... even during that time, I still heard my name being called in the stairwell. And I was still completely convinced that the cameras in the hallways were being used to track me. So the mood was better, but those other things didn't go away.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports a chronic depressive syndrome (low mood, anergia, guilt, anhedonia) present nearly continuously for over a year, with psychotic symptoms (auditory hallucinations of hearing her name, persecutory delusions about surveillance cameras) emerging about a month later and persisting for ~11 months. Critically, she describes a several-week period when her mood clearly improved (better appetite, improved work functioning) yet the hallucinations and delusional beliefs about being watched persisted unchanged. This confirms that psychotic symptoms occur independent of mood episodes for a substantial period (>2 weeks), ruling out a mood disorder with psychotic features (F32.3), while the fact that mood symptoms have been present for the majority of the total illness duration (most days over 14 months) argues against primary schizophrenia (F20.9). This pattern—overlapping mood and psychotic symptoms with a demonstrated period of psychosis without mood disturbance, combined with mood symptoms present for a majority of the illness course—meets criteria for schizoaffective disorder, depressive type.
